title: Typed merge problem instance (SCHEMA_V1)
description: A finite positive conjunctive authority system: claims, a finite license universe, seed labels, capped rules, and directly refuted claims. Encode your own domain in this schema to evaluate it with typed_merge_evaluator; no evaluator code needs to change. The operator evaluated is F_R(x)_q = {} if q in R, else sigma(q) union the union over rules with head q of (cap_r intersect the intersection of the body labels); Auth(R) is its least fixed point.

schema.description: Schema identity tag. Must be exactly this string.

id.description: Stable identifier for this instance, unique within a corpus.

provenance.description: Free-form record of where this encoding came from. Carries no semantics for the evaluator, but a third party should be able to trace every claim and license back to a source artifact.

licenses.description: The finite license universe Lambda. A license is whatever independent authority must carry a derivation end to end: an evidence class (THEOREM, FINITE_EXACT, PROSPECTIVE, ...), an origin store, a signing record, a source repository. The calculus is indifferent to which; it only requires that the set be finite and declared.

seeds.description: sigma: the independent seed label of each claim. Omitted claims have the empty seed label. Every license named here must appear in `licenses`.

rules.description: Positive conjunctive rules. Bodies must be non-empty: a zero-antecedent rule is a seed and must be written as one.

id.description: Unique rule identifier; defaults to rule<index>.

body.description: Antecedent claims A. All must hold for the rule to transfer anything.

cap.description: The rule cap K_r: the licenses this rule is permitted to transmit. The string "ALL" expands to the declared license universe. A cap is how nonpromotion is stated: a rule that must not confer PROSPECTIVE simply omits it from the cap, and then no proof tree through that rule can carry it.

refuted.description: R, the directly refuted claims. Their label is forced to the empty set regardless of any derivation.

flat_seeded_claims.description: Optional override of the seed set used by the license-erased (flat) evaluation. Null, the default, means the flat pass seeds exactly the claims with a non-empty typed seed, so typed and flat differ only by license erasure. Supply an explicit list only when the modelled flat merge is additionally less faithful than license erasure alone -- for example a textual concatenation that also drops the retraction material the typed view honours. Any such divergence must be justified in `provenance`. This field overrides SEEDS ONLY: claims listed in `refuted` are refuted in both the typed and the flat reading, and no value here can change that.

targets.description: Claims to report on. Defaults to every claim. Each must appear in `claims`.

expect.description: Optional declared expectations. The evaluator compares its output against these and reports every mismatch; this is what makes an instance a regression test rather than a demonstration.

pairs.description: The exact claim-license pairs of A_pre \ A_post.
